name: Red Calcite
physical: Traditionally linked to vitality and stamina
Associated with a warm, lively feeling
Kept nearby by many for energy and motivation
summary: Red calcite is a warm brick-red carbonate tinted by iron, and crystal lore links it to vitality, courage and grounded, practical motivation.
intro: Red calcite is a brick, rust or terracotta colored carbonate, usually translucent with a soft waxy glow and sometimes streaked with white or orange. The red tone comes from traces of iron oxide dissolved into the stone as it formed, which explains why it sits close in color to red jasper though it is far softer. It is generally sold as tumbled stones, spheres, hearts and raw chunks, and its cheerful warmth makes it a popular choice for people who want an energizing stone without jewelry-level cost. The stone feels slightly waxy and cool in the hand and warms up quickly with contact.
history: Calcite has been used since ancient times as a building stone, for carving and as a source of lime, and its red varieties turn up wherever iron-bearing waters pass through limestone or marble. Mexico and Brazil are major sources of the red material seen in the crystal trade. Because it is so soft and easy to carve, red calcite has been shaped into small animal figures, beads and ornaments for decades. In modern crystal practice, color is used as a guide to chakra, so red calcite was adopted as a root chakra stone, taking on the fiery, grounding associations of red stones in general.
meaning: Red calcite is a stone of vitality and grounded courage. Practitioners link it to the root and sacral chakras, and use it to wake up sluggish energy, kickstart a stalled project or find the nerve to begin. It is described as warm, practical and encouraging, especially for people who feel flat, drained or overly cautious. The calcite family is often considered an energy amplifier, and red calcite is thought to supercharge the drive of the stone it is paired with. Traditionally it is associated with stamina, warmth and a lively mood, and it is commonly kept nearby during the colder months or while recovering from busy stretches.
howToUse: Carry a red calcite tumbled stone in your pocket when you need an extra push, and hold it in your hand before a workout, a hard conversation or a big task. Place a sphere or chunk on a workspace in the south of your home or office to energize the area. In a root chakra layout, lay a piece at the base of the spine while lying down, breathing slowly into the belly. Combine with carnelian for creativity and with black tourmaline for protected, grounded energy. A small stone makes a thoughtful gift for someone starting something new.
care: Red calcite is soft at 3 and reacts to acids, so avoid vinegar, lemon and harsh cleaners. Keep it dry rather than soaking it, since water can dull the surface. Wipe with a soft dry cloth. Cleanse with smoke, sound, moonlight or a bed of selenite. Avoid strong sunlight, which can fade the color. Store it wrapped in cloth, away from harder stones, and avoid hard knocks because it chips easily.
identify: Genuine red calcite is soft enough to scratch with a copper coin or knife and will fizz if a drop of weak acid touches it. Red jasper is harder, more opaque and takes a glassier polish; carnelian is translucent and harder still. Dyed calcite shows color that collects in cracks and looks unnaturally bright. Natural pieces usually have subtle variation, streaks and cloudy areas, so uniformly vivid red should be questioned.

faq.q: What is red calcite good for?
faq.a: Practitioners use red calcite for vitality, courage and practical motivation. Its warm red is linked to the root chakra and is often carried to help start tasks, stay active or feel more grounded.

faq.q: Can red calcite go in water?
faq.a: It is best kept dry. Calcite is soft and reacts to acids, and water can dull the polish over time. Wipe it with a soft cloth and cleanse with smoke, sound or moonlight instead of soaking.

faq.q: How is red calcite different from red jasper?
faq.a: Red calcite is a soft carbonate that fizzes in acid and scratches easily, while red jasper is a hard, opaque quartz variety. Both are warm and grounding in crystal lore, but jasper is much more durable.
